still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false and the first filer's 180-day exclusivity is still parked behind the 2033 FDA warning letter on its Telangana plant.
The permanent Part D obesity benefit still pays the $199/month negotiated rate with a $50 beneficiary copay, eligibility at BMI ≥30 or ≥27 with one comorbidity, plus the counselling visit.

The CMS continuation standard is unchanged (≥80% PDC, six-monthly verified weights, 5% response or clinician override, annual DEXA for long-term 65+ users, the 90-day 'bone pause' code, and two misses suspend coverage for 6 months), and the same 31 states plus DC use it for the 90% Medicaid match.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.

The FTC consent orders still stand: 'Quiet', 'Even' and 'Unhooked' may say 'calm' and 'focus' but may not claim to treat anxiety. The 'Safe Pens' authentication bill is still stalled and Congress has passed no importation law.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Adults ≈277M. Current users 28.3% ≈78.4M. Ever-used 42.5% ≈117.7M, up 2.5 pts (limit 2.8). Never-used 57.5% ≈159.3M. Off now: 42.5 − 28.3 = 14.2 pts ≈39.3M, up from 11.5 pts. Cycling: ≈15.5 pts of current users are on a second or later course and ≈5.0 pts of the off-now group restarted at least once and stopped again, so (15.5 + 5.0)/42.5 ≈ 48.2%. That is consistent with ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Why current use is flat (−0.2 pts) while ever-use rises: imported and counterfeit users fell from ≈7.1M to ≈5.7M after China's Apr 2035 export licensing on peptide APIs doubled gray prices to $45–70. Of the ≈1.4M who left, ≈0.6M moved to $149 portal starter pills and ≈0.8M stopped. The anhedonia label (Jun 2035) produced ≈0.3M net stops among 'calm' and standard-dose users. These losses are offset by top-third growth (retatrutide, MariTide, and ≈0.42M on the new bimagrumab combination) and by ageing into Medicare. Age check (band populations 52/92/61/72M): 18–29: 15% = 7.8M; 30–49: 31.5% = 29.0M; 50–64: 42% = 25.6M; 65+: 22.3% = 16.1M. Total ≈78.5M ≈ 28.3%. Income thirds: (32.5 + 29 + 23.4)/3 = 28.3. The bottom third fell 1.1 pts on the import squeeze and the top rose 0.5. The off-now 39.3M is concentrated among bottom-third adults in non-expansion states, people who were gated or tenure-lapsed, older users on bone pauses, NAION workups or post-NAION stops, and a new group of label-driven quitters who cite 'the grey'. Pediatric: 1.3% of ≈73M ≈950k, of whom ≈840k are adolescents 12–17 and ≈110k are children 6–11 on weekly semaglutide since the Oct 2035 approval, two-thirds of them through Medicaid EPSDT. About two children in five live with at least one parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. Statute unchanged: Part D obesity benefit at the $199 negotiated rate, $50 copay, counselling visit. Medicare pays 19.0% of fills, ≈14.9M users (≈13.6M aged 65+ and ≈1.3M disabled under-65): ≈6.5M for diabetes and ≈8.4M for obesity. Obesity-benefit gross: 8.4M × $199 × 12 ≈ $20.1B. Copays: 8.4M × $50 × 12 ≈ $5.0B, so the program pays ≈$15.0B. All Medicare incretin fills: 14.9M × $2,388 ≈ $35.6B gross. In Nov 2035 CMS ruled that bimagrumab is not an 'anti-obesity medication' under the benefit statute. The muscle-preserving add-on is therefore not covered at $199, and Medicare beneficiaries cannot get it except by paying cash. Medicaid pays 14.9% of fills, ≈11.7M users × $2,388 ≈ $27.9B gross before supplemental rebates, in the same 31 states plus DC. EPSDT now covers ages 6–11 under the new label. The Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's 12-month lockout waiver in Feb 2036.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands. Domestic prices rose from $5–30 to $9–40 after China's Apr 2035 API licensing squeezed intermediates, and a production-linked incentive scheme is funding domestic peptide API, which is 12–18 months from scale. China: domestic generics continue, but export of GLP-1 APIs and Fmoc-protected building blocks needs a MOFCOM licence, and licences are granted slowly and selectively. Canada: generic semaglutide CAD 55–85. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt also have generics. Vietnamese and Turkish 'research' vial sellers fill part of the US parcel gap. US: the mid-2035 contingent date for rival filers passed with no launch, because of the Sept 2035 preliminary injunction on Novo's crystalline-form patent and an FDA forfeiture ruling that has still not come. The Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide imports from firms without US fill-finish would also apply to Indian generics on entry.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Prices stalled: no list or direct-portal price moved between 2034 and 2036. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $249–329; Wegovy pill 50 mg $299; oral starters $149–150; retatrutide $449 direct and $1,649 list; amycretin $499; MariTide $549 month-equivalent. New: the bimagrumab add-on is $899/month direct, and the co-packaged tirzepatide + bimagrumab kit lists at $2,190. PBM net ≈$195–215, flat. Gray pens rose from $20–30 to $45–70. Payer mix of ≈78.4M users: commercial 37.0% (29.0M); Medicare 19.0% (14.9M); Medicaid 14.9% (11.7M); cash/direct 21.8% (17.1M, including ≈4.8M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers and most of the ≈0.42M bimagrumab users); imported/counterfeit 7.3% (5.7M). Sum: 29.0 + 14.9 + 11.7 + 17.1 + 5.7 = 78.4M = 100%. There is no structural change in who pays. About 88% of covering employers now gate, about a third add tenure gates, and ≈40% of gated plans require 'Verified Adherence' connected caps or pens. About 15% of covering plans cover bimagrumab, and only with a DEXA lean-mass criterion. Routes: ≈40% of users are on daily orals; injectables still dominate top-tier regimens.

GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, incl. 12 mg)
GLP-1 + amylin analogue combination, weekly injectable (CagriSema)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide; MASH added Aug 2035)
GIPR-antagonist/GLP-1 agonist antibody-peptide conjugate, monthly injectable (MariTide)

Activin type II receptor antibody, monthly subcutaneous, co-administered with tirzepatide (bimagrumab, approved Apr 2036 for lean-mass preservation during incretin weight reduction; also co-packaged kit)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill incl. 50 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: pediatric obesity ages 6–11 with severe obesity (semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly, Oct 2035, specialist initiation, bone-age and DEXA monitoring)
lean-mass preservation during incretin weight reduction (bimagrumab + tirzepatide, Apr 2036)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm', 'focus' and 'craving freedom' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, ≈4.8M subscribers), now carrying both the NAION and anhedonia warnings
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens, now adding bimagrumab in concierge practices
bimagrumab without weight loss among physique and over-60 'hold' users
gray-market 'research' retatrutide, increasingly from Vietnamese and Turkish sellers
gambling and compulsive-shopping craving reduction, still anecdotal
drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. muscle_preserving_combo: Lilly filed tirzepatide + bimagrumab in Feb 2035 on phase 3 data: ≈21% mean weight loss, with lean mass ≈10% of total loss on DEXA against ≈35% on tirzepatide alone. FDA approved it in Apr 2036, 14 months after filing, which is inside the 12-month rule. The label states lean-mass preservation. It does not claim fracture or falls reduction, and handgrip and chair-rise gains were modest and not statistically significant against tirzepatide alone. A functional-outcomes trial in over-65s is a postmarketing requirement. Marketing says 'Hold what you've built.' pediatric_under_12: semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly was approved for ages 6–11 in Oct 2035 on a 68-week RCT (BMI reduction ≈−17% vs placebo), with growth, puberty and bone-accrual PMRs. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Aug 2035. Lilly's next-generation orals are still unfiled. No US generic. Incretin market ≈$200B: US ≈$176B (≈72.7M paying users × ≈$202 net × 12 ≈ $176B), ex-US ≈$24B, flat as Indian and Chinese prices rose.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Bimagrumab adds diarrhoea in some users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; severe gastroparesis caution retained.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ population and high-dose regimens.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Gray product still confounds reporting.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL ongoing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈1.8M long-term older users meet sarcopenia criteria in Medicare claims. Bimagrumab cuts the lean share of loss to ≈10% on DEXA, but only ≈0.42M people are on it, mostly cash-paying top-third users under 65. Medicare beneficiaries, who have the most sarcopenia, are largely excluded by the CMS non-AOM ruling.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label and body-composition monitoring retained. CMS annual DEXA requirement unchanged. CMS Nov 2035 ruling: bimagrumab is not covered under the obesity benefit.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈8.0M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 8.0M × ~0.6%/yr × 0.35 excess ≈ 16,800 excess hip fractures a year, against ~310,000 US total. The vertebral tail in cycling women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–14 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints required in all filings; 90-day bone-pause code unchanged; DOJ civil case against Novo unresolved.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Relative risk ≈1.7 across the class. ≈78M users × 4/100,000 × 0.7 ≈ 2,200 excess cases a year, mostly partial and permanent monocular loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions since May 2034; MDL consolidated in 2035; no boxed warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association, and the 2035 pooled analysis again found none.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Warning removed Jan 2026; not returned.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening / anhedonia ('Ozempic personality', 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. In Jun 2035 FDA pooled 14 RCTs that used prospective SHAPS and OQESA measures. Clinically meaningful anhedonia was 3.1% at standard maintenance doses vs 1.2% on placebo, 8.4% at 12 mg retatrutide vs 2.9%, and 1.9% vs 1.2% at low oral starter doses, the last not significant in any single trial. Excess cases implied: ≈8.5M top-dose users × 5.5% ≈ 470k; ≈60M standard-dose users × 1.9% ≈ 1.1M; ≈4.8M 'calm' subscribers × 0.7% ≈ 34k. Total ≈1.6M. Most cases resolve within 8–12 weeks of dose reduction.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions plus an Adverse Reactions table with prevalence, and a Medication Guide line ('about 3 in 100 people'). Not boxed. Prescribers are advised to screen at dose escalation. The FTC consent orders are unchanged, so subscription brands may keep 'calm' as long as the warning is displayed.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Import-squeeze stops (≈0.8M) and label-driven stops add to gating, tenure-gap and bone-pause stops.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code unchanged. Seventh Circuit upheld the Indiana waiver Feb 2036.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Common in high-loss older users, in gray-market users, and now under watch in 6–11-year-olds.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Professional guidance; Part D counselling screen; pediatric label requires a dietitian at initiation.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent readout shows BMD z-score gain ≈0.2 SD lower than placebo at 2 years. Whether that persists to peak bone mass is unknown. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Adolescent label updated with the bone-accrual finding; peak-bone-mass PMR extended to 2041.

safety_ledger.effect: Pediatric 6–11: growth velocity, pubertal timing, disordered eating
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. About 110k children are exposed. Trial data showed no height-velocity difference at 68 weeks, but the trial was too small to detect pubertal-timing or eating-disorder signals.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Specialist initiation, bone-age X-ray and DEXA at baseline, an ED screening tool in the label, and a 10-year registry PMR.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Imported users fell from ≈7.1M to ≈5.7M, but sourcing has scattered to new Vietnamese and Turkish sellers and stretched dilutions. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are roughly flat on 2034. Two smaller contamination clusters (≈60 hospitalisations, 2 deaths) were recorded in 2035–36.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: More import alerts; seizures up. Safe Pens still stalled. Individuals still not prosecuted.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded. Pressed tablets now make up about a third of seized product, at 0–300% of labelled content. Hypoglycaemia in insulin users is the main serious harm.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use, with NAION a cofactor in a minority of cases. Very few of these patients are on bimagrumab.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Concentrated among over-50s who were gated, tenure-lapsed, or squeezed off imports in 2035.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Joint society guidance published 2035; no regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Several bpm rise at 12 mg retatrutide. The CV outcomes trial has not read out.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Precautionary label.

safety_ledger.effect: Activin-pathway effects (bimagrumab): muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne, unknown long-term effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. Muscle spasm in ~25% early on and acne in ~10%. Long-term cardiac and reproductive effects are unknown beyond 72 weeks. Off-label use without weight loss among physique users is growing.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; contraception advice; long-term safety PMR.

safety_ledger.effect: Strength–function gap (lean mass preserved without matching strength or function)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New entry. In the bimagrumab trial, DEXA lean mass was preserved but handgrip and chair-rise gains were small. Geriatricians warn that 'solved' sarcopenia is a DEXA result, not yet a falls result.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label limited to lean mass; functional-outcomes PMR in over-65s.

food_and_beverage.state: Use is flat at about 28%, so the decline has slowed. Salty-snack volume falls ~3% a year and confectionery ~4%. The price-tier split has hardened. Premium 'hold' protein lines are marketed alongside bimagrumab, discount grocers on Phoenix's west side push calorie-dense value packs to people squeezed off imports, and the first school-lunch reformulation pilots respond to the 6–11 indication.

alcohol.state: Eighth straight year of spirits volume decline. Beer is down too. Non-alcoholic formats hold. Distillers lobby against the anhedonia framing because 'quiet' marketing competes with the drink as a wind-down.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat and spend per cover still ~10% below 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced bowls are standard. Rural value buffets keep their modest recovery among off-drug diners.

apparel.state: Class sizing has deepened. Premium brands in Scottsdale and Buckhead add 'hold' cuts for bimagrumab bodies that are thinner without the soft arm. Discount 'cycle' ranges expand. A children's 'growth-flex' line from one mid-market chain was criticised and pulled within a month.

fitness.state: Mixed. Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' keeps growing because Medicare users cannot get bimagrumab. Premium 'regimen management' gyms lose some members who now 'hold' pharmacologically and stop lifting. DEXA chains gain bimagrumab monitoring visits.

insurance.state: Employer coverage is 63%. About 88% of covering plans are gated, and ≈40% of those require Verified Adherence connected caps or pens. Pharmacy trend has slowed to ~+6% (flat price, flat volume). Few plans cover bimagrumab. Life insurers now ask about adherence data. Bone, fall and NAION costs land on Part A and Medicare Advantage.

pharma.state: Volume is flat and net price flat. US incretin revenue is ≈$176B. Lilly is the designated Strategic Peptide Supplier with a DPA Title III award and leads on retatrutide, tirzepatide, Foundayo and bimagrumab. Novo holds oral share with the 50 mg pill and defends semaglutide with the crystalline-form patent. Amgen sells MariTide. Indian generic makers are squeezed by Chinese API licensing and the 100% Section 232 peptide tariff.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, now at finer grain. The top tier has a 'hold' body: thin, with arms that did not soften, from bimagrumab with tirzepatide or a coached retatrutide regimen. The middle has the soft 'pill body' of the 50 mg pill on a gated plan with a blinking smart cap. Visible cycling and the thin-armed stoop read as Medicaid lockouts, tenure gaps, or the import squeeze of 2035.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use converges by income, with the bottom third at 23.4% against 32.5% at the top, while bodies diverge further. Women 50–64 are still the most visibly sorted group. In Phoenix, Scottsdale women 'hold' on cash bimagrumab at $899 a month, while Maryvale women who lost $25 Indian pens in 2035 regained fat-dominant and wait out tenure gates. Medicare women over 65 cannot buy back muscle at any covered price.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first shared meals among users. Sunday full-table dinners and church potlucks in Memphis and Houston remain the places where off and cycling families eat. Parents of 6–11-year-olds on weekly pens debate whether birthday cake is a dose question, and school nurses keep dose logs.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Profiles say 'holding' or 'coached', and both are read as income. Some profiles now list 'no grey' after the label. 'Unmedicated' is a stable niche.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised among the insured and treated as a supply problem among the rest. The backlash coalition is about the same size. After the pediatric approval, a parents' wing formed in suburban Texas and Ohio. Its focus is children, not price.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. The label now gives prevalence: 3.1% vs 1.2% at standard maintenance doses, 8.4% vs 2.9% at 12 mg retatrutide, and 1.9% vs 1.2% (not significant) at low oral starter doses. That implies ≈1.6M excess clinically meaningful cases across ≈78M users, most reversible with dose reduction. ≈4.8M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers carry the warning. Their excess rate is small and statistically fragile, which the brands quote. Counterfeit tablets at 0–300% of label add unmeasured exposure.
interior_life.framing: The label made it official, and the brands absorbed it. 'Quiet' rewrote onboarding: 'About 2 in 100 people feel less pleasure. Many of them came for exactly that.' Prescribers say 'anhedonia, labelled'. Users still say 'the grey', and some now say 'I'm on the label', meaning they have it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: 'Focus' subscriptions stay in lifestyle catalogues at most large white-collar employers. A minority of employers dropped them after the label, citing liability. Verified Adherence caps make dosing visible to plan vendors, and unions in warehousing and call centres bargain to have anhedonia dose reductions coded as medical holds rather than adherence misses. Sales staff still dose down before quarter-end.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Grey era' is now a clinical phrase as well as a genre label. Musicians in Nashville and Austin who write 'off label' market the label. High-stimulus leisure grows. A documentary about a Dayton family's import pens after the China controls played on the festival circuit.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists screen against the label's adverse-reaction table. Couples negotiate dose-downs for anniversaries. Partners of 'calm' subscribers ask whether the quiet is the drug or the marriage, and the label now gives them a number to argue over.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The 2036 presidential race treats incretins as a supply-security issue. 'Peptide sovereignty' is a bipartisan applause line, the Lilly DPA award is defended as industrial policy, and populists attack the 100% tariff as a tax on poor people's pens. The pediatric approval energised a parents' bloc. The Safe Pens bill is still stalled.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding. It labelled anhedonia with prevalence and approved 6–11 semaglutide and bimagrumab with functional and growth PMRs. It added import alerts and has still not ruled on the first filer's generic forfeiture. CMS excluded bimagrumab from the $199 obesity benefit. The FTC consent orders stand. There is no importation or authentication law.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: Unchanged in structure: permanent Part D benefit at $199 with a $50 copay; 90% Medicaid match for the 31 states plus DC; EPSDT obliges coverage for 6–11-year-olds in all Medicaid states. No individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deepened without new payers. The CMS continuation standard is unchanged. The Seventh Circuit upheld Indiana's 12-month lockout in Feb 2036, and Arkansas kept its rule. A Dec 2035 DOL/HHS/Treasury FAQ affirmed that plans may require connected-device adherence data (smart caps, connected pens) as a coverage condition and premium-tier input inside the existing 30% wellness allowance. A top-three PBM's 'Verified Adherence' programme is now in ≈40% of gated plans, so dosing timestamps, kiosk weights and connected-scale data feed premiums.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and fleets keep voluntary visual-field checks. After the anhedonia label, some fleets added a mood screen at medical recertification; FMCSA issued no rule. Army accession policy is still contested and Air Force waivers continue. DPA Title III treats domestic peptide capacity as a defence-industrial asset.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Politicised. In Apr 2035, after US Section 232 pharma tariffs, China put GLP-1 APIs and Fmoc building blocks under export licensing. Commerce answered with a 100% tariff on finished peptide imports from firms without US fill-finish, and HHS named Lilly a Strategic Peptide Supplier with a DPA award and a stockpile contract. India calls both the Telangana import alert and the tariff protectionism, and is subsidising domestic API. The gray market shrank and scattered to new sources.

events.event: China adds GLP-1 peptide APIs and Fmoc-protected amino-acid intermediates to its export-licence list in retaliation for US Section 232 pharma tariffs. Within weeks Commerce sets a 100% tariff on finished peptide drugs from makers without US fill-finish, and HHS names Eli Lilly a 'Strategic Peptide Supplier' with a Defense Production Act Title III award. Gray-market pen prices double to $45–70

FDA adds anhedonia and emotional blunting to every GLP-1-class label with a prevalence table from 14 pooled trials: 3.1% vs 1.2% placebo at maintenance doses and 8.4% at 12 mg retatrutide. 'Quiet' and 'Even' keep selling 'calm' under the unchanged FTC orders and rewrite onboarding around the number

The mid-2035 entry date for rival generic semaglutide passes with no launch. A Delaware federal court grants Novo a preliminary injunction on a crystalline-form patent, and FDA still has not ruled on whether the parked first filer forfeited its 180-day exclusivity. Analysts now pencil in 2037, and no brand price has moved since 2034

FDA approves weekly semaglutide 2.4 mg for children aged 6–11 with severe obesity, requiring specialist initiation, bone-age and DEXA monitoring, and a 10-year growth registry. Medicaid EPSDT coverage follows automatically, and about 110,000 children are on it by late 2036

The Seventh Circuit upholds Indiana's Medicaid waiver that locks people out for 12 months after two missed verifications. The same month a top-three PBM's 'Verified Adherence' programme, which requires smart caps or connected pens for gated employer coverage and was cleared by a Dec 2035 tri-agency FAQ, reaches about 40% of gated plans

FDA approves Lilly's bimagrumab for use with tirzepatide, 14 months after a Feb 2035 filing. Lean mass is about 10% of weight lost versus about 35% on tirzepatide alone, with no functional benefit proven. It costs $899/month direct and $2,190 list for the kit. CMS has already ruled it outside the $199 obesity benefit, and Scottsdale gyms advertise 'Hold what you built'

open_tensions: Muscle preservation is now for sale, but CMS has excluded it from the $199 benefit. Medicare holds the most sarcopenic and fracture-prone users (≈16,800 excess hip fractures a year), and the only people protected are those paying cash, so the 'skinny-frail' problem is solved mostly for those under 65 with $899 a month. Whether DEXA lean mass translates into fewer falls is unproven.

Supply is now industrial policy. China's API licensing, the 100% peptide tariff and Lilly's national-champion status shrank the import market from 7.1M to 5.7M users. The rest scattered to less-known sellers, and the parked generic, which would itself be tariffed, is still blocked by a patent injunction and an FDA forfeiture decision that has not come.

Anhedonia is labelled at 2–3 in 100, and the same effect is sold as 'calm' to ≈4.8M people with no weight indication. Verified Adherence now records their dosing for employers' plan vendors, and nobody has defined whether a dose-down for the grey counts as a missed dose.

About 110k children aged 6–11 started weekly semaglutide inside households where two in five parents cycle. The adolescent data already show slower bone accrual, so what happens to their growth and appetite before peak bone mass is a question only the 2040s can answer.

prose.headline: Holding Pattern: America stalls at 28% on the drug, prices freeze, and the rich buy back their muscle at $899 a month
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 the number of American adults on an incretin drug has stopped moving. It is twenty-eight percent, as it was two years ago. Underneath the flat line, about a million people left the gray market, roughly as many arrived at the top, and children joined for the first time.

The gray market shrank because of geopolitics. In April 2035, after another round of American pharmaceutical tariffs, Beijing put the raw materials of the peptide trade under export licence: the active ingredients and the protected amino acids that Indian factories turn into pens. Washington answered with a hundred-percent tariff on finished peptide drugs from companies with no American fill-finish line, and named Eli Lilly a strategic supplier under the Defense Production Act. The twenty-five-dollar Hyderabad pen became a sixty-dollar pen from a seller nobody had heard of. About six hundred thousand people moved to the $149 starter pills on the federal portal. About eight hundred thousand simply stopped, and their waistlines show it.

Prices for everyone else did not move. The generic semaglutide that was due in mid-2035 is still not here. A Delaware court enjoined the rival filers on a crystal-form patent, and the FDA has never decided whether the first filer, parked since 2033 behind a warning letter, lost its head start. Medicare still pays $199 and charges a $50 copay. Employers still pay about two hundred a month net, and they keep adding conditions. A large pharmacy-benefit manager now requires a connected cap on the bottle or a connected pen in four of ten gated plans, so the timestamp of each dose reaches the plan vendor alongside the kiosk weight. Regulators issued an FAQ saying this is allowed. In February the Seventh Circuit said Indiana's twelve-month lockout is allowed too.

In June 2035 the FDA did what it had resisted for years and put a number on the grey. Pooled trials found that about three users in a hundred on maintenance doses develop clinically meaningful anhedonia, against one in a hundred on placebo, and more than eight in a hundred at the top triple-agonist dose. At the low doses sold for calm, the excess is small and fragile. The subscription brands built their marketing on that fragility. Quiet's onboarding now says that some people feel less pleasure and many came for exactly that. Nearly five million people subscribe.

In October the drug reached children aged six to eleven with severe obesity, by weekly pen, under specialist care with bone-age films and a ten-year registry. Medicaid covers it by law. About a hundred and ten thousand children are on it. The parents' movement against it is loud in suburban Texas and Ohio, and quiet everywhere else.

In April Lilly sold the answer to the skinny-frail body. An antibody given monthly alongside tirzepatide keeps the muscle that weight loss used to take: on a scan, a tenth of the loss is lean tissue instead of a third. The trial could not show that people got stronger. The price is $899 a month on top of the shot. Medicare ruled that it is not an anti-obesity drug and will not cover it, so the people with the most fragile bones can only watch the advertisements.

The result is a new body at the top. In Scottsdale and Buckhead the 'hold' body is thin without the soft upper arm, and the shops cut jackets for it. In Maryvale the regain after a lost import shows around the middle over thin arms. Women in their fifties are sorted most visibly, by plan design more than by willpower. Nothing collapsed, nobody marched, and the curve is flat.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorena Vásquez wakes at 4:50 in Maryvale and twists the cap off the 50 mg bottle. The cap blinks green. Somewhere a vendor logs 4:51.

She manages the cafeteria at a district elementary school. Her plan covers the pill because she passed her twelve months last spring, and because the cap keeps blinking. Her sister Marisol lost her pens in 2035. They went from twenty-five dollars to sixty overnight, and now Marisol stands differently.

At work Lorena portions turkey chili into the new reformulated trays. A third-grader named Teo comes through the line with a nurse's note clipped to his lanyard: Saturday dose, small portions, no seconds without asking. She gives him the apple anyway.

At lunch she reads the insert she ignored in June. About 3 in 100 people. She thinks about Christmas, when her granddaughter opened the presents and Lorena felt it the way you feel weather through a window. She refolds the paper the way it came.

On the bus home along Indian School, a billboard shows a woman her age in a sleeveless dress. HOLD WHAT YOU BUILT. $899. Lorena looks at her own forearm, which is thin and loose at the elbow.

Marisol comes over for Sunday-style dinner on a Thursday and brings tamales. Lorena eats one slowly. Marisol eats four, then cries a little, then laughs about crying.

At 9:40 Lorena's phone buzzes: Weigh-in due in 6 days at your nearest kiosk. She sets the bottle beside the sink where the cap can see her.

least_plausible_claims.quote: In Nov 2035 CMS ruled that bimagrumab is not an 'anti-obesity medication' under the benefit statute.
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: CMS rules on coverage status for a drug that FDA did not approve until Apr 2036, five months later. The coverage exclusion that anchors the main inequality story is not shown to have a causal chain.

Magnitude and mechanism: 0.42M users at $899/month, mostly cash-paying, within about eight months of an Apr 2036 approval, with 15% of plans covering it, is an implausibly fast ramp. It is also listed as an offset to current-use change over a window that begins in 2034.

least_plausible_claims.quote: A top-three PBM's 'Verified Adherence' programme is now in ≈40% of gated plans
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: one PBM cannot plausibly reach 40% of all gated employer plans within about two months of a Dec 2035 FAQ. Smart-cap and connected-pen requirements need hardware logistics and contract cycles, and the jump is asserted rather than shown.

rationale.badness: The world keeps every 2034 harm and adds more. It carries about 1.6M excess anhedonia cases, about 16,800 excess hip fractures a year, and about 2,200 NAION cases a year. Connected-cap dosing timestamps now feed employer plans, Indiana's 12-month lockout is upheld, and 110k children aged 6–11 are on the drug. Muscle preservation is sold at $899/month while Medicare is excluded. The harm is also now named and quantified on the label, which keeps epistemic badness moderate. Overall this is a society most readers would refuse to live in if they understood it, though not structurally invisible.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All ten drivers appear in fields and dated events. Adoption is −0.2, prices are stalled, the tariff shock is Apr 2035, the anhedonia label is Jun 2035, bimagrumab is filed Feb 2035 and approved 14 months later, and the pediatric under-12 approval is Oct 2035. None is contradicted. mechanism: The tariff, import squeeze and gray-market shift chain is well shown. The pre-approval CMS ruling, the 40% PBM penetration and the 0.42M bimagrumab ramp are asserted (claims 1–3). Pharmacy trend falling to +6% with flat price and flat volume is also unexplained. magnitude: Population is inside the envelope (28.3% current, 42.5% ever), and the age, income, payer-mix, Medicare and Medicaid dollar and market arithmetic all reconcile. The bimagrumab approval at 14 months respects the 12-month rule. Minor gaps: the off-now rise of about 7.5M is only partly explained, and the 0.42M uptake is fast.
rationale.generativity: The day in the life of Lorena Vásquez is strong: the blinking cap, the vendor logging 4:51, the nurse's note on Teo's lanyard, the HOLD WHAT YOU BUILT billboard, and Marisol with the tamales. Fields supply place-specific texture such as Maryvale versus Scottsdale, parents' wings in Texas and Ohio, and unions bargaining over coding of dose-downs.
